title: The shard key picks one shard; the router knows which
caption: A small, cached shard map turns the key into a shard. Each shard is an ordinary database with its own replicas.

steps.text: Every query carries the shard key (here user_id). The router can be a library inside the app or a proxy in front of the shards.
The router maps key → shard with the shard map: key ranges, hash slots or a lookup table. The map is tiny and cached, so this costs microseconds.
The query goes to exactly one shard. The other shards never see it, so adding shards adds capacity.
Each shard holds a disjoint slice of the rows and has its own replicas. Shards share nothing, which is the point and also the problem: no joins or transactions across them.
